tools.name: companies
tools.description:
Count, filter and rank SCVS company financial statements; use this for company numbers.

All filters are optional. Amounts are USD, employees is a count. `ciiu` accepts a code prefix
('A0119') or a Spanish sector word ('flores'); word matches report the matched codes. CIIU
describes activity, not ex

tools.name: search
tools.description:
Find passages in every document Ecuadorian public institutions publish. Start research here.

For company counts, rankings, revenue, size or employees call `companies` and cite its `source`.

`query`: words or a question, best in Spanish, as the documents are ("inversión extranjera en
minería", "Dec

tools.name: fetch
tools.description:
Read one document, or one passage in its context, by the id `search`, `documents` or `citations` gave.

A passage id (the `id` of a search result) returns the document's card and that passage with
the one before and after it. A document id (`document_id`) returns the document's text,
verbatim, with

tools.name: read
tools.description:
Read part of a long document: a range of pages, or one article.

Pass `document_id` and either `page_from` (and optionally `page_to`), as `fetch`'s `next`
suggests, or `article` ('15', 'Art. 15', 'primero', 'único') for that article's full text,
however many pages it spans. `max_chars` is at most 40

tools.name: citations
tools.description:
What a document cites, amends or repeals, or which documents cite, amend or repeal it.

`direction`: 'out' (default) for the instruments this document refers to - the law it applies,
the articles it amends, what it repeals, the rulings it cites; 'in' for the documents in the
corpus that refer to thi

tools.name: documents
tools.description:
List documents newest first, without a query: "the latest resolutions of the SRI", "what
did the Registro Oficial publish in March 2024", "recent ordinances on mining".

Filters as in `search`, each optional, one value or several comma-separated: `family`,
`kind`, `category` (normativa | comunicacio

tools.name: catalog
tools.description:
What exists: every publisher (family) with how many documents it has and how many have text.

Call it to learn the valid `family` keys and the kinds each publisher prints before filtering
`search` or `documents`, or to judge whether a missing answer means a gap in the corpus.
`sector` narrows to one

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "companies" appears informational but accepts parameters (history) that enable code/file/secret access.

evidence.snippet: year, revenue_min, revenue_max, assets_min, employees_min, employees_max, ciiu, province, ruc, name, sort, limit, offset, history

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search, fetch, read, citations, documents · Private data: companies, search, fetch, read, citations, documents, catalog · Public sink: search, documents.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search, fetch, read, citations, documents · Private data: companies, search, fetch, read, citations, documents, catalog · Public sink: search, documents

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
